texts.text: (A) The Parties have entered into a Master Services Agreement dated 15 January 2026 (the "MSA") under which the Processor provides the Controller with a hosted e-commerce analytics platform (the "Services").

texts.text: (C) The Parties enter into this DPA to satisfy the requirements of Article 28(3) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (the "GDPR").

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 1. DEFINITIONS
texts.text: 1. DEFINITIONS

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 1.1 Capitalised terms not otherwise defined in this DPA have the meanings given to them in the MSA.
texts.text: 1.1 Capitalised terms not otherwise defined in this DPA have the meanings given to them in the MSA.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 1.2 "Personal Data", "Data Subject", "Processing", "Personal Data Breach", "Supervisory Authority" and "Technical and Organisational Measures" have the meanings given in the GDPR.
texts.text: 1.2 "Personal Data", "Data Subject", "Processing", "Personal Data Breach", "Supervisory Authority" and "Technical and Organisational Measures" have the meanings given in the GDPR.

texts.label: text

texts.text: 1.3 "Sub-processor" means any third party engaged by the Processor to process Personal Data on behalf of the Controller.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 2. SUBJECT MATTER AND DURATION
texts.text: 2. SUBJECT MATTER AND DURATION

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 2.1 This DPA governs the Processing of Personal Data by the Processor on behalf of the Controller in connection with the Services.
texts.text: 2.1 This DPA governs the Processing of Personal Data by the Processor on behalf of the Controller in connection with the Services.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 2.2 This DPA takes effect on the Effective Date and remains in force for as long as the Processor processes Personal Data on behalf of the Controller under the MSA.
texts.text: 2.2 This DPA takes effect on the Effective Date and remains in force for as long as the Processor processes Personal Data on behalf of the Controller under the MSA.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 2.3 The subject matter, nature and purpose of the Processing, the types of Personal Data and the categories of Data Subjects are set out in Annex 1.
texts.text: 2.3 The subject matter, nature and purpose of the Processing, the types of Personal Data and the categories of Data Subjects are set out in Annex 1.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 3. INSTRUCTIONS OF THE CONTROLLER
texts.text: 3. INSTRUCTIONS OF THE CONTROLLER

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 3.1 The Processor shall process Personal Data only on documented instructions from the Controller, including with regard to transfers of Personal Data to a third country, unless required to do so by Union or Member State law to which the Processor is subject.
texts.text: 3.1 The Processor shall process Personal Data only on documented instructions from the Controller, including with regard to transfers of Personal Data to a third country, unless required to do so by Union or Member State law to which the Processor is subject.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 3.2 If the Processor is required by law to process Personal Data beyond the Controller's instructions, it shall inform the Controller of that legal requirement before Processing, unless that law prohibits such information on important grounds of public interest.
texts.text: 3.2 If the Processor is required by law to process Personal Data beyond the Controller's instructions, it shall inform the Controller of that legal requirement before Processing, unless that law prohibits such information on important grounds of public interest.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 3.3 The Processor shall immediately inform the Controller if, in its opinion, an instruction infringes the GDPR or other Union or Member State data protection provisions.
texts.text: 3.3 The Processor shall immediately inform the Controller if, in its opinion, an instruction infringes the GDPR or other Union or Member State data protection provisions.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 4. CONFIDENTIALITY
texts.text: 4. CONFIDENTIALITY

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 4.1 The Processor shall ensure that persons authorised to process the Personal Data have committed themselves to confidentiality or are under an appropriate statutory obligation of confidentiality.
texts.text: 4.1 The Processor shall ensure that persons authorised to process the Personal Data have committed themselves to confidentiality or are under an appropriate statutory obligation of confidentiality.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 4.2 The confidentiality obligations under this Section 4 survive the termination of this DPA.
texts.text: 4.2 The confidentiality obligations under this Section 4 survive the termination of this DPA.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 5. SECURITY OF PROCESSING
texts.text: 5. SECURITY OF PROCESSING

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 5.1 Taking into account the state of the art, the costs of implementation and the nature, scope, context and purposes of Processing, the Processor shall implement and maintain the Technical and Organisational Measures set out in Annex 2.
texts.text: 5.1 Taking into account the state of the art, the costs of implementation and the nature, scope, context and purposes of Processing, the Processor shall implement and maintain the Technical and Organisational Measures set out in Annex 2.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 5.2 The Processor shall ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk, including, as appropriate, pseudonymisation and encryption of Personal Data, the ability to ensure ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems, and a process for regularly testing, assessing and evaluating the effectiveness of the measures.
texts.text: 5.2 The Processor shall ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk, including, as appropriate, pseudonymisation and encryption of Personal Data, the ability to ensure ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems, and a process for regularly testing, assessing and evaluating the effectiveness of the measures.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 5.3 The Processor may update the Technical and Organisational Measures from time to time, provided that such updates do not materially reduce the overall level of protection.
texts.text: 5.3 The Processor may update the Technical and Organisational Measures from time to time, provided that such updates do not materially reduce the overall level of protection.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 6. SUB-PROCESSING
texts.text: 6. SUB-PROCESSING

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 6.1 The Controller grants the Processor a general authorisation to engage Sub-processors for the Processing of Personal Data, subject to this Section 6.
texts.text: 6.1 The Controller grants the Processor a general authorisation to engage Sub-processors for the Processing of Personal Data, subject to this Section 6.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 6.2 The Sub-processors approved as of the Effective Date are listed in Annex 3.
texts.text: 6.2 The Sub-processors approved as of the Effective Date are listed in Annex 3.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 6.3 The Processor shall inform the Controller in writing of any intended addition or replacement of a Sub-processor at least 30 days before the change takes effect, thereby giving the Controller the opportunity to object to such changes.
texts.text: 6.3 The Processor shall inform the Controller in writing of any intended addition or replacement of a Sub-processor at least 30 days before the change takes effect, thereby giving the Controller the opportunity to object to such changes.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 6.4 If the Controller objects on reasonable data protection grounds within 30 days of the notice, the Parties shall discuss the objection in good faith; if no resolution is reached, the Controller may terminate the affected part of the Services without penalty.
texts.text: 6.4 If the Controller objects on reasonable data protection grounds within 30 days of the notice, the Parties shall discuss the objection in good faith; if no resolution is reached, the Controller may terminate the affected part of the Services without penalty.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 6.5 The Processor shall impose on each Sub-processor, by way of a written contract, data protection obligations that are no less protective than those set out in this DPA, and the Processor remains fully liable to the Controller for the performance of each Sub-processor's obligations.
texts.text: 6.5 The Processor shall impose on each Sub-processor, by way of a written contract, data protection obligations that are no less protective than those set out in this DPA, and the Processor remains fully liable to the Controller for the performance of each Sub-processor's obligations.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 7. ASSISTANCE WITH DATA SUBJECT RIGHTS
texts.text: 7. ASSISTANCE WITH DATA SUBJECT RIGHTS

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 7.1 Taking into account the nature of the Processing, the Processor shall assist the Controller by appropriate technical and organisational measures, insofar as this is possible, for the fulfilment of the Controller's obligation to respond to requests for exercising the Data Subject's rights under Chapter III of the GDPR.
texts.text: 7.1 Taking into account the nature of the Processing, the Processor shall assist the Controller by appropriate technical and organisational measures, insofar as this is possible, for the fulfilment of the Controller's obligation to respond to requests for exercising the Data Subject's rights under Chapter III of the GDPR.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 7.2 The Processor shall notify the Controller of any request received directly from a Data Subject within 5 business days of receipt and shall not respond to such request itself, except on the documented instructions of the Controller.
texts.text: 7.2 The Processor shall notify the Controller of any request received directly from a Data Subject within 5 business days of receipt and shall not respond to such request itself, except on the documented instructions of the Controller.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 7.3 The Processor shall provide the assistance described in this Section 7 at no additional charge, unless the volume of requests is manifestly excessive.
texts.text: 7.3 The Processor shall provide the assistance described in this Section 7 at no additional charge, unless the volume of requests is manifestly excessive.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 8. PERSONAL DATA BREACH NOTIFICATION
texts.text: 8. PERSONAL DATA BREACH NOTIFICATION

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 8.1 The Processor shall notify the Controller without undue delay, and in any event no later than 48 hours, after becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach affecting Personal Data processed under this DPA.
texts.text: 8.1 The Processor shall notify the Controller without undue delay, and in any event no later than 48 hours, after becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach affecting Personal Data processed under this DPA.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 8.2 The notification under Section 8.1 shall, at a minimum, describe the nature of the Personal Data Breach, the categories and approximate number of Data Subjects and Personal Data records concerned, the likely consequences, and the measures taken or proposed to address the breach and mitigate its possible adverse effects.
texts.text: 8.2 The notification under Section 8.1 shall, at a minimum, describe the nature of the Personal Data Breach, the categories and approximate number of Data Subjects and Personal Data records concerned, the likely consequences, and the measures taken or proposed to address the breach and mitigate its possible adverse effects.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 8.3 The Processor shall document all Personal Data Breaches and shall cooperate with the Controller in relation to any notifications to Supervisory Authorities or communications to Data Subjects that the Controller determines are required.
texts.text: 8.3 The Processor shall document all Personal Data Breaches and shall cooperate with the Controller in relation to any notifications to Supervisory Authorities or communications to Data Subjects that the Controller determines are required.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 9. DATA PROTECTION IMPACT ASSESSMENTS
texts.text: 9. DATA PROTECTION IMPACT ASSESSMENTS

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 9.1 The Processor shall provide reasonable assistance to the Controller with any data protection impact assessments and prior consultations with Supervisory Authorities which the Controller reasonably considers to be required by Articles 35 and 36 of the GDPR, in each case solely in relation to the Processing of Personal Data under this DPA.
texts.text: 9.1 The Processor shall provide reasonable assistance to the Controller with any data protection impact assessments and prior consultations with Supervisory Authorities which the Controller reasonably considers to be required by Articles 35 and 36 of the GDPR, in each case solely in relation to the Processing of Personal Data under this DPA.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 10. AUDITS AND INSPECTIONS
texts.text: 10. AUDITS AND INSPECTIONS

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 10.1 The Processor shall make available to the Controller all information necessary to demonstrate compliance with the obligations laid down in this DPA and shall allow for and contribute to audits, including inspections, conducted by the Controller or an auditor mandated by the Controller.
texts.text: 10.1 The Processor shall make available to the Controller all information necessary to demonstrate compliance with the obligations laid down in this DPA and shall allow for and contribute to audits, including inspections, conducted by the Controller or an auditor mandated by the Controller.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 10.2 The Controller may conduct an on-site audit no more than once per calendar year, upon at least 30 days' prior written notice, during normal business hours and without unreasonably interfering with the Processor's business operations.
texts.text: 10.2 The Controller may conduct an on-site audit no more than once per calendar year, upon at least 30 days' prior written notice, during normal business hours and without unreasonably interfering with the Processor's business operations.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 10.3 Notwithstanding Section 10.2, the Controller may audit the Processor at any time following a Personal Data Breach or where required by a Supervisory Authority.
texts.text: 10.3 Notwithstanding Section 10.2, the Controller may audit the Processor at any time following a Personal Data Breach or where required by a Supervisory Authority.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 10.4 Each Party shall bear its own costs in connection with an audit under Section 10.2.
texts.text: 10.4 Each Party shall bear its own costs in connection with an audit under Section 10.2.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 11. INTERNATIONAL TRANSFERS
texts.text: 11. INTERNATIONAL TRANSFERS

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 11.1 The Processor shall not transfer Personal Data to a country outside the European Economic Area unless the transfer is subject to appropriate safeguards under Chapter V of the GDPR.
texts.text: 11.1 The Processor shall not transfer Personal Data to a country outside the European Economic Area unless the transfer is subject to appropriate safeguards under Chapter V of the GDPR.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 11.2 Where a transfer is based on standard contractual clauses adopted by the European Commission, the Parties shall execute such clauses, and this DPA shall be interpreted so as not to conflict with them.
texts.text: 11.2 Where a transfer is based on standard contractual clauses adopted by the European Commission, the Parties shall execute such clauses, and this DPA shall be interpreted so as not to conflict with them.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 11.3 As of the Effective Date, all Personal Data is stored in data centres located in Norway and Estonia.
texts.text: 11.3 As of the Effective Date, all Personal Data is stored in data centres located in Norway and Estonia.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 12. RETURN AND DELETION OF PERSONAL DATA
texts.text: 12. RETURN AND DELETION OF PERSONAL DATA

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 12.1 Upon termination or expiry of the MSA, the Processor shall, at the choice of the Controller, delete or return all Personal Data to the Controller within 90 days, and delete existing copies unless Union or Member State law requires storage of the Personal Data.
texts.text: 12.1 Upon termination or expiry of the MSA, the Processor shall, at the choice of the Controller, delete or return all Personal Data to the Controller within 90 days, and delete existing copies unless Union or Member State law requires storage of the Personal Data.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 12.2 Upon the Controller's request, the Processor shall certify in writing that it has complied with Section 12.1.
texts.text: 12.2 Upon the Controller's request, the Processor shall certify in writing that it has complied with Section 12.1.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 13. LIABILITY
texts.text: 13. LIABILITY

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 13.1 Each Party's aggregate liability arising out of or in connection with this DPA is subject to the limitations and exclusions of liability set out in the MSA, save that the aggregate liability of the Processor for breaches of this DPA shall not exceed EUR 500,000 or the total fees paid by the Controller under the MSA during the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to the claim, whichever is higher.
texts.text: 13.1 Each Party's aggregate liability arising out of or in connection with this DPA is subject to the limitations and exclusions of liability set out in the MSA, save that the aggregate liability of the Processor for breaches of this DPA shall not exceed EUR 500,000 or the total fees paid by the Controller under the MSA during the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to the claim, whichever is higher.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: 13.2 Nothing in this DPA limits either Party's liability for damages suffered by Data Subjects as provided under Article 82 of the GDPR.
texts.text: 13.2 Nothing in this DPA limits either Party's liability for damages suffered by Data Subjects as provided under Article 82 of the GDPR.

texts.text: 14. TERM AND TERMINATION

texts.orig: 14.1 This DPA commences on the Effective Date and terminates automatically upon expiry or termination of the MSA, subject to Section 12.
texts.text: 14.1 This DPA commences on the Effective Date and terminates automatically upon expiry or termination of the MSA, subject to Section 12.

texts.text: 14.2 Sections 4, 12 and 13 survive the termination of this DPA.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: B2. INCIDENT CLOCKS
texts.text: B2. INCIDENT CLOCKS

texts.label: text
texts.orig: B2.1 The 24-hour outer limit in A2.1 remains the standard initial-notification limit. For a breach confirmed to expose usable privileged credentials, the expedited outer limit is 12 hours from the original awareness of the breach, even if the credential exposure is confirmed later. An automated alert alone is not awareness; verified unauthorised access to Personal Data is awareness. Neither a change of incident classification nor later escalation restarts either clock. The duty to notify without undue delay remains; meeting an outer limit alone does not establish compliance with that separate duty.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: B2.2 A completed follow-up report is due by the end of the third Business Day after awareness. The initial notice and follow-up report are separate obligations; an incomplete report does not postpone initial notification. The content requirements in Section 8.2 and the cooperation duty in Section 8.3 continue to apply.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: B2.3 Only a Controller-approved pause can suspend the follow-up clock. Exclude only the whole Business Days expressly approved in writing, even if the Processor requested a longer interval. No pause suspends the initial-notification clock. Ignore a pause request that was refused or never approved.

texts.text: B3. DELETION AND LIMITED RETENTION

texts.label: text
texts.orig: B3.1 For terminations from 1 March 2027 onward, A5.1's ordinary deletion period remains applicable. A legal hold applies only to the identified records, including their copies. If several holds cover the same records, release occurs only when the last applicable hold ends. Delete those held records by the later of the ordinary deletion deadline and the end of the tenth Business Day after that release. A hold does not extend deadlines for any other records.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: B3.2 A backup containing no held records must be deleted by the earlier of its ordinary deletion deadline and 35 calendar days after its creation. A restore or an internal request to retain it does not restart this period. Section B3 controls in case of conflict with Annex 2's retention schedules.

texts.label: text

An internal request is not a Controller instruction and cannot extend a hold or authorise another use. After the ordinary deletion deadline, the hold and the deletion window following its release remain the sole retention authority for the held records.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: B4.1 For proposed additions or expanded processing from 1 March 2027 onward, Sections 6.3 and 6.4's notice process alone does not authorise the change. Approval begins no earlier than the proposed start date, completion of the security review, and written Controller consent, whichever is latest. All three conditions must be satisfied for the specific service and processing country. A consent limited to one service or country does not authorise another. Silence is not consent. Previously approved services remain approved unless expressly withdrawn.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: B5.1 The ordinary cap is EUR 1,000,000 per Contract Year. Breaches of Sections 5 or 8 instead share one separate security cap per Contract Year, equal to the greater of EUR 2,000,000 and twice Qualifying Fees for the event. A Contract Year runs from 1 March through the last day of the following February. Qualifying Fees are recurring service fees paid in the twelve complete calendar months preceding the event's month, excluding VAT, service credits and one-off training. A paid credit reduces the fees for its stated service period. Do not include fees for the event's month. The ledger amounts below are exhaustive and all in EUR.
